artifacts.summary: Six-phase implementation: a new git-commit-phase.sh wrapper (files_touched derivation + mechanized containment check + unpiped commit + post-commit completeness check), its 16-assertion fixture suite, migration of both phase-commit call sites in general-implementation-agent.md, a new piped-invocation lint rule wired into verify-deploy gate 17, and corrections to three durable records (Verification's issues.jsonl, git-staging-scope.md's ten-vs-nine Typst miscount, and task 374's inverted commit-provenance issue-log entry). completion_data.completion_summary: Added git-commit-phase.sh, a mechanized phase-commit wrapper that derives the stage list from a phase's own files_touched and fails loudly (exit 6) when a derived path is not clean against HEAD after the commit, closing the caller-side omission that silently dropped zigzag.typ from commit fc9f786e. Migrated both phase-commit call sites, mechanized a piped-invocation lint rule, and corrected three durable records that carried disproven claims about the incident.

memory_candidates.content: A test assertion of the shape `if upstream_cmd | grep -q PATTERN; then` can falsely report failure under `set -o pipefail`: grep -q closes its read end as soon as it finds a match, which can SIGPIPE the still-writing upstream process; pipefail then reports the pipeline's exit status as that SIGPIPE kill (141) rather than grep's own successful 0, even though the match genuinely occurred. This is a race that gets MORE likely (not less) as the upstream's trailing output grows, so adding even a couple of harmless summary lines to a passing script can flip a previously-passing assertion to a deterministic failure with no logic change. Fix: capture the upstream's output into a variable first (`out="$(upstream_cmd)"; grep -q PATTERN <<< "$out"`) rather than piping directly into `grep -q` whenever the test suite also sets `set -o pipefail`.

When a prose self-check instruction documented in an agent contract is explicitly flagged as 'an interim measure, not a claimed permanent fix' pending a mechanical home, and later work needs to actually mechanize it, the correct home is often a NEW wrapper script sitting in front of the existing sanctioned script, rather than editing the existing script's own semantics -- especially when the existing script's own staging/exit-code contract is explicitly out of scope to change. The wrapper can derive inputs (e.g. a stage list) the inner script never had access to, perform the self-check mechanically, then delegate to the inner script unmodified. This mirrors the update-phase-status.sh precedent (a prose heartbeat instruction fired 0/8 times; moving the identical step inside a script every caller must already invoke fired 16/16).
